output.sql:
WITH cat_rev AS (
  SELECT p.category,
         SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date) = 2024 THEN l.net_amount ELSE 0 END) AS rev_2024,
         SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date) = 2025 THEN l.net_amount ELSE 0 END) AS rev_2025
  FROM marts.fct_order_lines l
  JOIN marts.fct_orders o ON o.order_id = l.order_id
  JOIN marts.dim_products p ON p.product_id = l.product_id
  WHERE o.is_revenue
    AND o.order_date >= DATE '2024-01-01'
    AND o.order_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY p.category
)
SELECT category,
       ROUND(rev_2024, 2) AS revenue_2024,
       ROUND(rev_2025, 2) AS revenue_2025,
       ROUND(rev_2025 - rev_2024, 2) AS revenue_increase
FROM cat_rev
ORDER BY rev_2025 - rev_2024 DESC
LIMIT 1;
output.explanation: This query finds the category whose revenue grew the most from 2024 to 2025, and shows both years' totals and the increase. The figures are sums of line-level net amounts (after discounts), counting only orders where is_revenue is true, as the business definition requires. Each order is assigned to a year by its order date, and lines are grouped into categories through dim_products. None of the tables has a currency column, so I've assumed all amounts are in EUR and no conversion is needed. If two categories tie for the biggest increase, only one is returned.
